codeReview.summary: The implementation adds ProxyConfig and ProxyPool structs to the Rust backend with comprehensive unit tests (48 proxy tests passing). The code follows Rust conventions, properly integrates with the check-if-email-exists library via to_check_email_proxy(), and includes Tauri commands for proxy management. The implementation matches all expected behaviors: ProxyConfig has host/port/username/password fields with JSON serialization, ProxyPool has proxies/enabled/rotation_mode/domain_assignments, and comprehensive tests cover parsing, validation, pool management, and domain assignments.

summary: PASS. The proxy-config-struct feature is well-implemented with comprehensive unit tests (48 tests), proper error handling, and correct integration with the check-if-email-exists library. ProxyConfig and ProxyPool structs support all required fields (host, port, username, password, enabled, rotation_mode, domain_assignments) with JSON serialization using camelCase. The Tauri commands for proxy management are properly registered. Minor clippy warnings exist for unused methods (dead_code) which is expected since this is the foundational struct - these will be used by later features. The implementation correctly handles edge cases like IPv6 addresses, authentication validation, duplicate detection, and case-insensitive domain assignments.
